content:
# my question
There will be creative projects that Training Adam does for memorialization, there will also be homeschooling projects, and then there will also be office administrative stuff we have to do. How should I categorize getting mechanical pencils for homeschooling stuff versus getting mechanical pencils for office admin?


# AI answer 
Categorizing purchases like mechanical pencils comes down to item tracking, intended deployment, and budget allocation, rather than the physical nature of the item itself. Because a mechanical pencil is identical whether used for an administrative desk or a student's desk, the distinction depends entirely on usage context and accounting design.
1. The Accounting Framework: Expense Categories
From a bookkeeping perspective, you will set up your Chart of Accounts to separate general operational overhead from program delivery:
 * Office Administrative: Categorize under General & Administrative (G&A) Expenses \rightarrow Office Supplies.
   * Purpose: Overhead required to keep the nonprofit functioning (e.g., meeting notes, board documentation, administrative work).
 * Homeschooling: Categorize under Program Services / Educational Supplies \rightarrow Branch Supplies (or specific branch line items like Rethinking Human or Grow Up and Play).
   * Purpose: Direct material costs used to deliver your educational or community-focused programs.
2. Practical Ways to Categorize & Track Purchases
Option A: Receipt Line-Item Split (Single Purchase)
If you buy a box of 50 mechanical pencils at the store on a single receipt:
 * Divide the cost based on allocation (e.g., 10 pencils for administration, 40 pencils for homeschooling).
 * When logging the receipt into your accounting software (or submitting for reimbursement), split the transaction into two distinct ledger entries:
   * $10.00 \rightarrow G&A: Office Supplies
   * $40.00 \rightarrow Program: Homeschool / Educational Supplies
Option B: Separate Receipts at Checkout (Easiest Paper Trail)
If you want to keep the audit trail completely clean and hassle-free:
 * Ring up the office administrative supplies on Transaction #1.
 * Ring up the homeschooling/program supplies on Transaction #2.
 * Keep the separate receipts attached to their respective reimbursement or expense tracking forms.
Option C: Physical Labeling & Storage
 * Office Admin Pencils: Stored in the administrative supply cabinet or kept with official office gear.
 * Homeschool Pencils: Stored in the dedicated homeschooling bin, learning space, or program kit.
3. Why This Separation Matters for Your Non-Profit
 * IRS Form 990 Reporting: On Form 990, 501(c)(3) organizations are required to split functional expenses into Program Services, Management/General, and Fundraising. Clear categorization ensures you show a high percentage of expenses going directly toward your program delivery.
 * Grant & Earmarked Funding: If a donor or grant explicitly gives money to support your homeschooling or educational programs, you must show that purchases made with those funds (like homeschooling pencils) directly serve program participants rather than general overhead.
